channel.title: Newsnavigator (English)
channel.description: We deliver the news. What you make of it is up to you.

item.title: COP31 climate summit in Antalya runs into overtime amid dispute over fossil fuels
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, has gone into overtime. Several sources report disagreement over how to handle fossil fuels, and the summit presidency says, according to Reuters, that it hopes to reach consensus on a new package. (Sources: Deutsche Welle, The Japan Times, The Hindu, ABC News (Australien), The Straits Times)

item.title: Trump threatens to block or tax US firms building AI data centres abroad
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Trump said on Friday that US companies building AI data centres overseas could be blocked or face a very high tax. According to the BBC, he gave few details about the proposal, and others in his team reportedly heard about it for the first time. (Sources: The Daily Caller, MercoPress, South China Morning Post, The Guardian, El País América)

item.title: Merz: European leaders could join new Ukraine talks soon
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says European leaders could join new Ukraine talks soon. The United Arab Emirates is named as a possible location, according to The Straits Times. (Sources: The Hindu, Daily Maverick, Hindustan Times, The Wall Street Journal, RT)

item.title: European countries expect to join new Ukraine talks, says Merz
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says European leaders could join new Ukraine talks soon, according to Deutsche Welle. At a meeting in Berlin, European allies of Ukraine say they have a united negotiating position, BBC reports. (Sources: BBC World, Politico Europe, Meduza, The Hindu, France 24)

item.title: Israel launches ground operation in central Gaza
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Israel's military has launched a ground operation in central Gaza, according to several outlets, with tanks crossing the so-called yellow line. The Japan Times reports that the body overseeing the truce says both Israel and Hamas have not met their commitments. (Sources: France 24, Middle East Eye, Sveriges Radio Ekot, The Guardian, BBC World)

item.title: Five EU countries plan return hub in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. According to several outlets, five EU countries, including Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, plan a return hub in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers. The UN human rights chief and Human Rights Watch express concern. (Sources: Al Jazeera, The East African, Africanews, Deutsche Welle)

item.title: Finland's president urges European leaders to talk directly with Putin
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Finnish President Alexander Stubb urges European leaders to talk directly with Putin, according to Yle, Kyiv Independent and Financial Times. Yle and Kyiv Independent report that he calls relying on the United States for Russia-Ukraine talks irresponsible. (Sources: Sveriges Radio Ekot, Politico Europe, The Straits Times, Yle News, Dagens Nyheter)

item.title: US introduces rules limiting Chinese firms' remote access to AI chips
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Tom's Hardware reports new US rules aimed at blocking Chinese firms' remote access to AI chips. CNA reports that data centres anywhere need a US licence to supply large computing volumes to firms headquartered in China and other countries, and China criticises the move. (Sources: CNBC, Hindustan Times, The Hindu, The Information, Nikkei Asia)

item.title: EU expands Russia sanctions to oil refineries, banks and Wildberries chief
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. According to Meduza, the EU has expanded its Russia sanctions list to include oil refineries, petrochemical plants and dozens of banks. Deutsche Welle reports that the EU has frozen assets of Wildberries chief Tatyana Kim and imposed a travel ban on her to the bloc. (Sources: France 24, Fox News, Rappler, The New York Times, The Washington Post)

item.title: California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face attack
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. California has sued OpenAI in connection with an attack on Hugging Face, according to several sources. According to Hindustan Times, the state seeks a court order requiring OpenAI to stop violating the law and to pay for the violations. (Sources: Ars Technica, DR Nyheder, CyberScoop, NPR, Breakit)

item.title: Five European countries plan return hubs for rejected asylum seekers in Rwanda
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Five European countries, Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands, plan to send rejected asylum seekers to a return hub in Rwanda. According to Premium Times, an initial pilot is expected to involve about 100 people, and human rights groups have criticised the plans. (Sources: Hindustan Times, El País América, Le Monde (English))

item.title: Trump says he may meet Kim Jong Un in China
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Trump says he may meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, according to Yonhap and The Straits Times. Arab News reports that China says it has no information about such a meeting. (Sources: Middle East Eye, Hindustan Times, Dawn, The Straits Times, Washington Examiner)

item.title: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant runs on generators again after losing external power
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. The Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant in Ukraine has lost its external power supply and is again running on backup power from generators, according to reports. The IAEA says the cause and location of the disconnection are not yet known. (Sources: The Hindu, The Straits Times, Dagens industri, Nikkei Asia)
